# dsh-omni-modal
**Give a text-only model the ability to draw pictures and shoot videos — without touching a single l
ine of DeepSeek Harness source.**
`dsh-omni-modal` adds an **Omni-modal settings** section to the DSH settings sidebar, where you can
point the harness at any **OpenAI-compatible** image / video endpoint and register three model-visib
harness at any **OpenAI-compatible** image / video endpoint and register three model-visible tools:
| Tool | What it does |
| `generate_image` | Synchronous text-to-image. Saves the PNG/JPEG/WebP to disk and (when the attach

ment service is available) returns an inline preview card. |
| `generate_video` | Asynchronous submi

t. Returns a task id immediately — the clip is still rendering. |
| `check_video` | Poll that task;
on success it downloads the finished video to disk. |
Status: usable, tracks the Harness developer preview — interfaces may change.
## Features
- **Live-editable settings page** — a real DSH settings section (not a static skill). Change endpoin
t, key, model, path or default size and hit **Save**; the three tools pick it up on their next call,

no restart.
- **Multiple config profiles** — keep several endpoints side by side, name them, switch
the active one at a time. Every tool also accepts an optional `profile` argument to use a non-activ

e profile for a single call.
- **Separate image and video configuration** — the two APIs rarely shar
e a shape. Each profile carries an independent `baseUrl` / `apiKey` / `model` / path / size for each

side.
- **Extra request parameters** — a free-form JSON object merged into the request body, for en

dpoint-specific knobs (`{"quality":"high"}`, `{"mode":"text","aspect_ratio":"16:9"}`, …).
- **Connec
tivity test** — one click probes `GET <baseUrl>/models` (falling back to the base URL itself) withou

t spending generation quota.
- **Async video by design** — submit, remember the task, poll later. Ta

sk records survive restarts.
- **No build step** — plain ESM host half plus a hand-written CJS clien
t bundle. Nothing to compile, no bundler needed.
## Install
Requires Node.js ≥ 18 and DeepSeek Harness.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`<profile>` is your DSH profile name (`web`, `desktop`, …). Add `#v0.1.0` to pin a tag.
Then **restart DSH** — the host half registers its routes and tools at boot, and the settings sectio
n appears under **Settings → Omni-modal settings**.
### Manual install (no pnpm / offline)
Copy this repository somewhere permanent, then add it to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
and mirror the same entry into the `importers.` → `dependencies` block of `pnpm-lock.yaml`, then cre
e same entry into the `importers.` → `dependencies` block of `pnpm-lock.yaml`, then create the link:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
> **Never copy the package into `node_modules` instead of linking it.** DSH uses a `Symbol` as the c
ross-module call key; loading the module twice makes those symbols unequal and every tool call then
throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`, with no recovery after a restart.
## Usage
Once installed, just talk to the agent:

- *"Draw a strawberry on a pale blue plate."* → `generate_image`
- *"Make a short video of a paper b
oat drifting down a stream."* → `generate_video`, then `check_video`
### Settings page
| Section | Contents |
| Config profiles | Pick the active profile, rename it, add one (copied from the current) / delete o

ne |
| Image | Base URL, API key, model, request path, default size, extra request params |
| Video
| Base URL, API key, model, submit path, query path, default resolution, default duration, extra req

uest params |
| Task records | Submitted video tasks with their status and artifact path |
Notes:

- **Saving takes effect immediately** for the tools — no restart.
- **The base URL must be the addre
ss alone.** Documentation examples are easy to copy verbatim as `POST https://api.example.com/v1`; t
he plugin strips a leading `POST`/`GET`/… automatically, but writing just `https://api.example.com/v

1` is safer.
- **The query path accepts two forms**: a relative path (`/videos/generations/{id}`) ap
pended to the base URL, or a **full URL** (`https://api.example.com/agnesapi?video_id={id}&model_nam
e={model}`) used as-is. The full form is necessary when the query endpoint does not live under the b

ase URL.
- Placeholders available in the query path:
| Placeholder | Replaced with |

| `{id}` | the task id returned by the submit call |
| `{model}` | the model name configured in that

the task id returned by the submit call |
| `{model}` | the model name configured in that profile |
- The tools **always use the active profile** unless you pass `profile` explicitly.
### Tools
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- `generate_image` returns synchronously. The file lands in the plugin data directory's `media/` and
, if the attachment service is available, an image attachment is produced so the picture shows up in
the conversation. **The model itself cannot see the pixels** — to actually look at the image, call

`read_image` on the returned path.
- `generate_video` is asynchronous: it returns a `taskId` right a
way. Call `check_video(task_id)` later; when the status becomes `succeeded` the artifact is download

ed into `media/` automatically.
- Passing a **non-existent profile is a hard error** that lists the
available profiles, rather than silently falling back to another one — otherwise the model would qui

etly use the wrong endpoint and model while the result still claims the profile it asked for.
- `che
ck_video` failures are **soft failures**: a missing task (404), an unreachable download URL or a fai
led download return `status: "failed"` / `"succeeded"` plus a `message`, instead of throwing. These

are expected business outcomes, and throwing would abort the whole tool-calling round.
- Video URL e
xtraction covers the common response shapes: `video_url` / `videoUrl` / `url`, nested `video.url`, `

data.*`, `output.*`, `result.*`, `videos[0].url`, and more.
